fr: Les enfants adorent le sport collectif.
en: Children love team sports.
ipa: le.zɑ̃.fɑ̃ a.dɔʁ lə spɔʁ kɔ.lɛk.tif
notes: The liaison between les and enfants turns into a clear z sound, so listen for lezenfants as one flowing unit.

fr: Je fais du sport chaque matin.
en: I do sport every morning.
ipa: ʒə fɛ dy spɔʁ ʃak ma.tɛ̃
notes: The final t in sport is never pronounced, so do not add a sound after the silent letter.

fr: Nous adorons les sports d'hiver.
en: We love winter sports.
ipa: nu.za.dɔ.ʁɔ̃ le spɔʁ di.vɛʁ
notes: Nous adorons is linked by a liaison z sound that makes the two words sound almost joined.

fr: Ils gagnent souvent leurs matchs.
en: They often win their matches.
ipa: il ɡaɲ su.vɑ̃ lœʁ matʃ
notes: The verb ending -ent in gagnent is completely silent, so the word sounds just like gagne.

fr: Vous êtes doués pour le tennis.
en: You are talented at tennis.
ipa: vu.zɛt dwe puʁ lə te.nis
notes: Vous êtes liaises with a z sound, linking the two words smoothly in speech.

fr: Le sport rend les enfants plus forts.
en: Sport makes children stronger.
ipa: lə spɔʁ ʁɑ̃ le.zɑ̃.fɑ̃ ply fɔʁ
notes: The final d in rend is silent, so nothing is heard after the nasal vowel.

fr: Mon ami arrive au club à midi.
en: My friend arrives at the club at noon.
ipa: mɔ̃.na.mi a.ʁiv o klœb a mi.di
notes: Mon ami liaises with an n sound, so it sounds like monami rather than two separate words.

fr: Nous marchons longtemps dans les bois.
en: We walk for a long time in the woods.
ipa: nu maʁ.ʃɔ̃ lɔ̃.tɑ̃ dɑ̃ le bwa
notes: The final s in bois is silent, so the word ends on the vowel sound alone.

fr: Ils habitent près du grand stade.
en: They live near the big stadium.
ipa: il.za.bit pʁɛ dy ɡʁɑ̃ stad
notes: The h in habitent is silent but still allows a liaison, so ils habitent sounds like ilzabitent.

fr: Il fait un temps idéal pour jouer.
en: The weather is ideal for playing.
ipa: il fɛ œ̃ tɑ̃ i.de.al puʁ ʒwe
notes: Both the p and the s in temps stay silent, leaving only the nasal vowel sound.

fr: Elles arrivent tôt pour le match.
en: They arrive early for the match.
ipa: ɛl.za.ʁiv to puʁ lə matʃ
notes: Elles arrivent liaises with a z sound that glides the two words together.

fr: Elle porte des gants chauds pour le ski.
en: She wears warm gloves for skiing.
ipa: ɛl pɔʁt de ɡɑ̃ ʃo puʁ lə ski
notes: The final t and s in gants are both silent, so only the nasal vowel is heard.

fr: Un athlète entraîne les jeunes joueurs.
en: An athlete trains the young players.
ipa: œ̃.na.tlɛt ɑ̃.tʁɛn le ʒœn ʒwœʁ
notes: Un athlète liaises with an n sound because the silent h in athlète does not block it.

fr: Les enfants courent vite sur le terrain.
en: The children run fast on the field.
ipa: le.zɑ̃.fɑ̃ kuʁ vit syʁ lə tɛ.ʁɛ̃
notes: The ending -ent of courent is silent, so the verb is pronounced exactly like court.

fr: Ces enfants aiment beaucoup nager.
en: These children love swimming a lot.
ipa: se.zɑ̃.fɑ̃ ɛm bo.ku na.ʒe
notes: Ces enfants is joined by a liaison z sound between the two words.

fr: Ils perdent rarement leurs matchs à domicile.
en: They rarely lose their home matches.
ipa: il pɛʁd ʁaʁ.mɑ̃ lœʁ matʃ a dɔ.mi.sil
notes: The -ent ending of perdent is silent, leaving the verb sounding like perd.

fr: Nos amis jouent au volley ce soir.
en: Our friends are playing volleyball tonight.
ipa: no.za.mi ʒu o vɔ.lɛ sə swaʁ
notes: Nos amis liaises with a z sound linking the plural possessive to the noun.

fr: Le corps a besoin de sport régulier.
en: The body needs regular exercise.
ipa: lə kɔʁ a bə.zwɛ̃ də spɔʁ ʁe.ɡy.lje
notes: Both the p and the s at the end of corps stay silent.

fr: Deux athlètes attendent le début du match.
en: Two athletes are waiting for the start of the match.
ipa: dø.za.tlɛt a.tɑ̃d lə de.by dy matʃ
notes: Deux athlètes liaises with a z sound linking the number to the noun.

fr: Elle regarde souvent les matchs à la télé.
en: She often watches the matches on TV.
ipa: ɛl ʁə.ɡaʁd su.vɑ̃ le matʃ a la te.le
notes: The final t in souvent is silent, so only the nasal vowel is heard before the next word.

fr: Les élèves apprennent à nager cet été.
en: The students are learning to swim this summer.
ipa: le.ze.lɛv a.pʁɛn a na.ʒe sɛ.te.te
notes: Les élèves liaises with a z sound joining the article to the noun.

fr: Nous jouons dans un grand champ derrière l'école.
en: We play in a big field behind the school.
ipa: nu ʒwɔ̃ dɑ̃.zœ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ ʃɑ̃ dɛ.ʁjɛʁ le.kɔl
notes: The final p in champ is completely silent, leaving only the nasal vowel sound.

fr: Son ami adore le football américain.
en: His friend loves American football.
ipa: sɔ̃.na.mi a.dɔʁ lə fut.bɔl a.me.ʁi.kɛ̃
notes: Son ami liaises with an n sound linking the possessive to the vowel-initial noun.

fr: Ils adorent le sport depuis leur enfance.
en: They have loved sport since childhood.
ipa: il.za.dɔʁ lə spɔʁ də.pɥi lœ.ʁɑ̃.fɑ̃s
notes: The -ent ending of adorent stays silent, so the verb sounds like adore.

fr: Vous allez au gymnase après l'école.
en: You go to the gym after school.
ipa: vu.za.le o ʒim.naz a.pʁɛ le.kɔl
notes: Vous allez liaises with a z sound that connects the pronoun to the verb.

fr: Elle a mal au dos après le sport.
en: Her back hurts after sport.
ipa: ɛl a mal o do a.pʁɛ lə spɔʁ
notes: The final s in dos is silent, so the word ends simply on the closed o sound.

fr: Trois enfants entrent dans la piscine.
en: Three children go into the pool.
ipa: tʁwa.zɑ̃.fɑ̃ ɑ̃tʁ dɑ̃ la pi.sin
notes: Trois enfants liaises with a z sound linking the number to the plural noun.

fr: Ce sport coûte cher pour les débutants.
en: This sport is expensive for beginners.
ipa: sə spɔʁ kut ʃɛʁ puʁ le de.by.tɑ̃
notes: The final t and s of débutants are both silent, leaving just the nasal vowel sound.

fr: Mes amis organisent un match amical.
en: My friends are organizing a friendly match.
ipa: me.za.mi ɔʁ.ɡa.niz œ̃ matʃ a.mi.kal
notes: Mes amis liaises with a z sound between the possessive and the noun.

fr: Ils dansent tous les vendredis soirs.
en: They dance every Friday evening.
ipa: il dɑ̃s tu le vɑ̃.dʁə.di swaʁ
notes: The -ent ending of dansent is silent, so the verb sounds identical to danse.

fr: Nous invitons un ancien joueur du club.
en: We are inviting a former player from the club.
ipa: nu.zɛ̃.vi.tɔ̃ œ̃.nɑ̃.sjɛ̃ ʒwœʁ dy klœb
notes: Nous invitons liaises with a z sound joining the subject pronoun to the verb.

fr: Elle porte toujours un legging gris pour courir.
en: She always wears grey leggings to run.
ipa: ɛl pɔʁt tu.ʒuʁ œ̃ le.ɡiŋ ɡʁi puʁ ku.ʁiʁ
notes: The final s in gris is silent, so the word ends on the vowel sound alone.

fr: Elle est allée à la piscine hier matin.
en: She went to the pool yesterday morning.
ipa: ɛl ɛ.ta.le a la pi.sin jɛʁ ma.tɛ̃
notes: Because aller takes être, the past participle allée adds a silent e to agree with the feminine subject elle.

fr: Il a couru à toute vitesse pendant le match.
en: He ran at full speed during the match.
ipa: il a ku.ʁy a tut vi.tɛs pɑ̃.dɑ̃ lə matʃ
notes: The verb form a and the preposition à sound identical, so only the accent distinguishes them in writing.

fr: Les joueurs ont gagné et on a organisé une fête.
en: The players won and we organized a party.
ipa: le ʒwœʁ ɔ̃ ɡa.ɲe e ɔ̃.na ɔʁ.ɡa.ni.ze yn fɛt
notes: Ont and on sound exactly the same, so listen to the sentence structure to know which spelling to write.

fr: Ils sont allés au club où ils s'entraînent le mardi.
en: They went to the club where they train on Tuesdays.
ipa: il sɔ̃.ta.le o klœb u il sɑ̃.tʁɛn lə maʁ.di
notes: Où meaning where is pronounced exactly like ou meaning or, so only context tells them apart.

fr: Le week-end, elle fait du sport ou elle se repose.
en: On weekends, she does sport or she rests.
ipa: lə wik.ɛnd ɛl fɛ dy spɔʁ u ɛl sə ʁə.poz
notes: Ou meaning or is a perfect homophone of où meaning where, so spelling depends purely on meaning.

fr: La joueuse que j'ai vue a marqué un but magnifique.
en: The player that I saw scored a magnificent goal.
ipa: la ʒwøz kə ʒe vy a maʁ.ke œ̃ by ma.ɲi.fik
notes: Because the direct object la joueuse comes before j'ai vue, the past participle vue must agree in the feminine.

fr: La salle de sport que nous avons visitée est très moderne.
en: The gym that we visited is very modern.
ipa: la sal də spɔʁ kə nu.za.vɔ̃ vi.zi.te ɛ tʁɛ mɔ.dɛʁn
notes: The preceding feminine object la salle forces the past participle visitée to take a silent extra e.

fr: On ira au stade si on a le temps demain.
en: We'll go to the stadium if we have time tomorrow.
ipa: ɔ̃.ni.ʁa o stad si ɔ̃.na lə tɑ̃ də.mɛ̃
notes: On a can sound like it could be written ont, so remember that on is always singular in form.

fr: Elle a fini son entraînement à huit heures.
en: She finished her training at eight o'clock.
ipa: ɛl a fi.ni sɔ̃.nɑ̃.tʁɛn.mɑ̃ a ɥi.tœʁ
notes: The verb a earlier in the sentence sounds just like the preposition à before huit heures.

fr: Mes sœurs sont arrivées en retard au tournoi.
en: My sisters arrived late to the tournament.
ipa: me sœʁ sɔ̃.ta.ʁi.ve ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ o tuʁ.nwa
notes: Since sœurs is feminine plural, the être past participle arrivées must take both a silent e and s.

fr: Il a couru cinq kilomètres ou il a fait du vélo.
en: He ran five kilometers or he went cycling.
ipa: il a ku.ʁy sɛ̃k ki.lɔ.mɛtʁ u il a fɛ dy ve.lo
notes: Ou here means or and sounds identical to où meaning where, so context decides the spelling.

fr: Les filles que j'ai entraînées ont bien progressé.
en: The girls that I coached have progressed well.
ipa: le fij kə ʒe ɑ̃.tʁɛ.ne ɔ̃ bjɛ̃ pʁɔ.ɡʁɛ.se
notes: The preceding plural feminine object les filles makes entraînées agree with a silent es ending.

fr: Nous irons au club où on joue au badminton.
en: We will go to the club where we play badminton.
ipa: nu.zi.ʁɔ̃ o klœb u ɔ̃ ʒu o bad.min.tɔn
notes: Où indicating a place sounds exactly like ou meaning or, so only the accent marks the difference.

fr: On a perdu le match mais on va s'entraîner plus.
en: We lost the match but we are going to train more.
ipa: ɔ̃.na pɛʁ.dy lə matʃ mɛ ɔ̃ va sɑ̃.tʁɛ.ne ply
notes: On a is easy to confuse with ont by ear, even though on always stays singular.

fr: Les blessures qu'elle a eues étaient graves.
en: The injuries she had were serious.
ipa: le blɛ.syʁ kɛl a y e.tɛ ɡʁav
notes: The preceding feminine plural object les blessures makes the past participle eues agree with a silent es.

fr: Il ira au gymnase à sept heures ce soir.
en: He will go to the gym at seven o'clock tonight.
ipa: il i.ʁa o ʒim.naz a sɛ.tœʁ sə swaʁ
notes: The preposition à here must not be confused with the verb form a, even though they sound the same.

fr: Les médailles qu'ils ont gagnées sont dans le salon.
en: The medals that they won are in the living room.
ipa: le me.daj kil ɔ̃ ɡa.ɲe sɔ̃ dɑ̃ lə sa.lɔ̃
notes: The preceding feminine plural object les médailles forces gagnées to agree with a silent es ending.

fr: Il faut que tu fasses du sport régulièrement pour rester en forme.
en: You need to do sport regularly to stay fit.
ipa: il fo kə ty fas dy spɔʁ ʁe.ɡy.ljɛʁ.mɑ̃ puʁ ʁɛs.te ɑ̃ fɔʁm
notes: The subjunctive fasses comes from an irregular stem and does not resemble the indicative fais at all.

fr: Je doute qu'elle soit assez rapide pour gagner la course.
en: I doubt she is fast enough to win the race.
ipa: ʒə dut kɛl swa.ta.se ʁa.pid puʁ ɡa.ɲe la kuʁs
notes: The subjunctive soit from être is a completely irregular spelling that must not be confused with soi or sois.

fr: Le coach veut que nous soyons prêts avant le match.
en: The coach wants us to be ready before the match.
ipa: lə koutʃ vø kə nu swa.jɔ̃ pʁɛ a.vɑ̃ lə matʃ
notes: The subjunctive form soyons is highly irregular and easy to misspell without hearing it clearly first.

fr: Il est important que vous ayez une bonne condition physique.
en: It is important that you have good physical fitness.
ipa: i.lɛ.tɛ̃.pɔʁ.tɑ̃ kə vu.ze.je yn bɔn kɔ̃.di.sjɔ̃ fi.zik
notes: The subjunctive ayez from avoir has an unusual spelling that does not match the indicative avez.

fr: Le professeur souhaite que tu ailles t'entraîner au stade.
en: The teacher wants you to go train at the stadium.
ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ swat kə ty aj tɑ̃.tʁɛ.ne o stad
notes: The subjunctive ailles from aller is entirely irregular and unrelated in spelling to vas or va.

fr: Il faudrait qu'ils puissent participer au tournoi ce weekend.
en: They would need to be able to take part in the tournament this weekend.
ipa: il fo.dʁɛ kil pɥis paʁ.ti.si.pe o tuʁ.nwa sə wik.ɛnd
notes: The subjunctive stem puiss- in puissent differs completely from the indicative stem peuv- in peuvent.

fr: Je ne pense pas qu'elle sache déjà nager aussi bien que lui.
en: I don't think she already knows how to swim as well as him.
ipa: ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kɛl saʃ de.ʒa na.ʒe o.si bjɛ̃ kə lɥi
notes: The subjunctive sache from savoir has a stem that does not resemble the indicative form sait at all.

fr: Ce joueur se blesse souvent pendant les matchs.
en: This player often gets injured during matches.
ipa: sə ʒwœʁ sə blɛs su.vɑ̃ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ le matʃ
notes: Ce the demonstrative and se the reflexive pronoun are perfect homophones, so grammar decides the spelling.

fr: Ces raquettes sont à elle, ses balles sont dans le sac.
en: These rackets are hers, her balls are in the bag.
ipa: se ʁa.kɛt sɔ̃.ta.ɛl se bal sɔ̃ dɑ̃ lə sak
notes: Ces and ses sound completely identical, so only the meaning of demonstrative versus possessive tells them apart.

fr: C'est son entraîneur qui choisit ses joueurs chaque semaine.
en: It is her coach who chooses her players every week.
ipa: sɛ sɔ̃.nɑ̃.tʁɛ.nœʁ ki ʃwa.zi se ʒwœʁ ʃak sə.mɛn
notes: C'est and ses are pronounced the same way, even though one is a verb phrase and the other a possessive.

fr: Quel sport préfères-tu pratiquer le weekend?
en: Which sport do you prefer to practice on weekends?
ipa: kɛl spɔʁ pʁe.fɛʁ ty pʁa.ti.ke lə wik.ɛnd
notes: Quel sounds exactly like its feminine form quelle, so only the gender of the following noun fixes the spelling.

fr: Quelle équipe a remporté le championnat cette année?
en: Which team won the championship this year?
ipa: kɛ.le.kip a ʁɑ̃.pɔʁ.te lə ʃɑ̃.pjɔ.na sɛt a.ne
notes: Quelle must agree with the feminine noun équipe even though it is pronounced identically to quel.

fr: Ce club se trouve près de chez ses parents.
en: This club is located near her parents' house.
ipa: sə klœb sə tʁuv pʁɛ də ʃe se pa.ʁɑ̃
notes: Ce, se and ses all share the same sound, so each spelling depends entirely on its grammatical role.

fr: C'est ce joueur qui s'entraîne le plus sérieusement.
en: It is this player who trains the most seriously.
ipa: sɛ sə ʒwœʁ ki sɑ̃.tʁɛn lə ply se.ʁjøz.mɑ̃
notes: C'est and ce sound alike but play very different grammatical roles in the sentence.

fr: Les athlètes ont eu un entraînement très intense hier.
en: The athletes had a very intense training session yesterday.
ipa: le.za.tlɛt ɔ̃.ty œ̃.nɑ̃.tʁɛn.mɑ̃ tʁɛ.zɛ̃.tɑ̃s jɛʁ
notes: The liaison in ont eu blends the two words so closely that the boundary between them is hard to hear.

fr: Ils ont assisté à un match extraordinaire au stade.
en: They attended an extraordinary match at the stadium.
ipa: il.zɔ̃.ta.si.ste a œ̃ matʃ ɛks.tʁa.ɔʁ.di.nɛʁ o stad
notes: The liaison in ont assisté makes the auxiliary and the participle sound almost like one continuous word.

fr: Nous avons appris à jouer aux échecs cet hiver.
en: We learned to play chess this winter.
ipa: nu.za.vɔ̃.na.pʁi a ʒwe o.ze.ʃɛk sɛ.ti.vɛʁ
notes: The chained liaisons in avons appris and aux échecs can make it easy to drop a syllable when writing.

fr: Les entraîneurs expérimentés observent attentivement chaque athlète.
en: Experienced coaches attentively observe each athlete.
ipa: le.zɑ̃.tʁɛ.nœʁ.zɛks.pe.ʁi.mɑ̃.te ɔb.zɛʁv a.tɑ̃.tiv.mɑ̃ ʃak a.tlɛt
notes: The liaison between entraîneurs and expérimentés can sound like an extra syllable was inserted.

fr: Elle est arrivée en avance pour éviter un grand embouteillage.
en: She arrived early to avoid a big traffic jam.
ipa: ɛ.lɛ.ta.ʁi.ve ɑ̃.na.vɑ̃s puʁ e.vi.te œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃.tɑ̃.bu.tɛ.jaʒ
notes: The liaison in en avance links the two words so tightly that the n can seem to belong to avance.

fr: Vous avez organisé un excellent événement sportif cette année.
en: You organized an excellent sports event this year.
ipa: vu.za.ve ɔʁ.ɡa.ni.ze œ̃.nɛk.se.lɑ̃.te.ve.nmɑ̃ spɔʁ.tif sɛt a.ne
notes: Two liaisons in a row in un excellent événement can blur where one word ends and the next begins.

fr: Ils ont hésité avant d'accepter cette invitation au tournoi.
en: They hesitated before accepting this invitation to the tournament.
ipa: il.zɔ̃.te.zi.te a.vɑ̃ dak.sɛp.te sɛt ɛ̃.vi.ta.sjɔ̃ o tuʁ.nwa
notes: The mute h in hésité still allows the liaison in ont hésité to sound like one smooth link.
